messages.author: 77a287453637d027
messages.subject: Re: Stan’s Within-Chain Parallelization
parts:
Hi David Munoz,

I've used within-chain parallelization of the latest Stan (with map_rect using cmdstanr) in my private projects. I ran my models to compute the log-likelihood for each participant with different CPU codes in a parallelized manner, and it was very helpful especially with datasets with large subjects in the multi-core server environment. However, it hasn't been applied to the codebase of hBayesDM yet.

Incorporating within-chain parallelization into hBayesDM seems to be a good idea, but I'm afraid there are several issues. For example, the current stan codes should be modified to use map_rect to calculate their likelihoods, and it would take time. Also, from some models in hBayesDM, users can extract model-based regressors. Those regressors may still require non-parallelized computations, which may not benefit from within-chain parallelization. Furthermore, within-chain parallelization may be applied across subjects, not across trials, because of dependencies in the data across trials from a subject. Due to this aspect, running hBayesDM with large-subject datasets can benefit from within-chain parallelization (as I did in my personal experiences), but it's unclear if it can also provide noticeable improvements even with usual cases in the subject number.

It would be great to incorporate within-chain parallelization into hBayesDM so that users who want to analyze large-subject datasets can benefit from its improvement. However, considering those issues I mentioned above, it seems to cost time to use it with hBayesDM yet.

Best regards,
Jaeyeong Yang
